data.title: Saudi Ground Services, EgyptAir Strengthen Strategic Partnership for Ground Handling Services at Saudi Airports
data.content:
Jeddah, November 21, 2026, SPA -- Saudi Ground Services (SGS) has strengthened its strategic partnership with EgyptAir, the national carrier of the Arab Republic of Egypt, by signing a contract to provide ground handling services for EgyptAir flights at all airports across the Kingdom. The agreement reinforces cooperation between the two companies and opens new opportunities to develop services and expand their partnership, keeping pace with the aviation sector's rapid growth and enhancing the passenger experience.
    The contract was signed by SGS Chief Executive Officer Mohammed Mazi and EgyptAir Chairman and CEO Captain Mohamed Alyan. The agreement reflects the two companies' commitment to developing ground handling services and leveraging their combined expertise and capabilities to meet operational requirements and passenger needs, while creating broader opportunities for future cooperation.
    The agreement covers a comprehensive range of ground handling services in accordance with the highest operational standards, focusing on two main areas. The first involves passenger services, including check-in procedures, boarding gate management, lounge services, baggage handling, and comprehensive passenger support.
    The second area covers ramp services, including loading and unloading operations, baggage handling, and the provision of various ground handling and support services required for aircraft on the apron. The agreement also includes exploring the provision of additional services at several airports across the Kingdom, contributing to an improved travel experience for EgyptAir passengers and creating new opportunities to expand cooperation and develop services in line with the two companies' future growth plans.
    The SGS CEO stated that the agreement represents a step toward expanding the partnership with EgyptAir and capitalizing on available opportunities to develop new areas of cooperation that generate sustainable value for both parties. He noted that the partnership extends beyond the provision of existing services to creating new opportunities for growth and development.
    He expressed SGS's commitment to exploring new areas of cooperation with EgyptAir and developing solutions that meet its future needs, enabling both companies to grow together and achieve tangible improvements in service quality and the passenger experience. He added that the agreement would strengthen a partnership model based on integration, knowledge exchange, and the creation of long-term value for both parties.
    -- SPA
